solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 25 down to 26); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: All but last of ice creams dished up in pots

indicators.note: food dished up is served out in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged
all but the last letter of the word ice is kept, dropping its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of ice

explanation.surface: Someone serves ice creams into little pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but last of' trims ICE to IC; 'dished up' rearranges IC plus CREAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottery is collectively called by this word, so a set of pots fits as an example.

clue.text: Rachel's new name after sex change?

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rachel takes a new name after changing sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RACHELS; a woman's name turns into a man's, hence the sex change.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name is what a Rachel might adopt after transitioning, so the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: Food from fish regularly taken from Rhone

indicators.note: every other letter of the river's name is picked out at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Food from fish is regularly caught in the Rhône.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly taken from' takes the first, third and fifth letters of RHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish eggs, the mass of them in a female fish, are eaten as food.

clue.text: Deception accomplished as short reservation's accepted

indicators.note: the outer word accepts the others inside it

parts.note: something accomplished has been made, achieved

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a reservation is a doubt or query

explanation.surface: A deception succeeded because a brief booking was accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservation' looks like a booking, which the surface suggests, but it is a doubt; the insert goes in straight after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A masked ball involves disguise, so the word extends to any pretence or show of deceit.

clue.text: First couple of clubs to admit entertainer

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the word clubs are taken

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so own means admit

explanation.surface: A couple of clubs let in an entertainer first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First couple of' gives CL from clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer in comic make-up is a classic entertainer.

clue.text: Go off on the trail of very old Times interviews

indicators.note: following behind, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
to pop is to go off with a bang, like a balloon

explanation.surface: A newspaper's interviews go off the rails after the old Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: A vox pop is a set of short street interviews with members of the public, from Latin vox populi.

clue.text: Reading out of letters hasn't paid off

indicators.note: reading words out means saying them aloud, so this is a sound-alike

parts.note: several of the letter O, written O's

explanation.surface: Someone reading out letters has not settled a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, O's (a run of the letter O) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor who still has something outstanding has not paid off what is due.

clue.text: What traitor did struck the wrong note

definitions.meaning: performed a wrong note on an instrument

explanation.surface: A traitor's act is likened to hitting a wrong note.
explanation.definitionFit: To act treacherously is idiomatically to be untrue, and a musician sounding an off note literally did so too.

clue.text: Scots borough blocking vote for salaried staff

indicators.note: the town sits inside the vote, blocking it

parts.note: a poll is a vote
Ayr is a town and royal burgh on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish borough blocks a vote on staff salaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of employees paid by a firm stands for its salaried staff.

clue.text: Lost land from biblical books, one in mountain range

indicators.note: the books and the one go inside the range

parts.note: the Atlas Mountains are a range in North Africa
NT is the New Testament, a set of biblical books
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lost land is described in biblical books, set in a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's legendary island sank beneath the sea, the archetypal lost land.

clue.text: People generally bearing blame after a model addict's treatment

indicators.note: the pronoun piece comes after the article and the model

parts.note: a model of a product is a version of it

indicators.note: carrying something within, so one word holds the other

parts.note: they, as in 'they say', means people in general
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: People blame an addict after copying a model's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a fashion model but means a version of something.
explanation.definitionFit: This conditioning method pairs a habit with something unpleasant, a known way of treating addiction.

clue.text: Italian in action with Hun and E European

indicators.note: things in action are moving about, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An Italian fights alongside a Hun and an Eastern European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action' rearranges ITALIAN plus HUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Baltic state centred on Vilnius is an Eastern European.

clue.text: Copyist's basic error not resolved — zeros overlooked

indicators.note: resolved here means broken up and reformed, so the letters are rearranged
the zeros are overlooked, missed out of the letters

parts.note: zero is written O, so two zeros are two of that letter

explanation.surface: A copyist's basic error is left unresolved, with the zeros missed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' drops the two O's from BASICERRORNOT; 'resolved' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes out copies of text, a scribe, is a copyist.

clue.text: Stoical leader of Japanese school finding love

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism strongly associated with Japan
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A calm head of a Japanese school finds love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoical' looks like a description of the leader's temperament, but the leader is the founder of the Stoics.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Citium founded the Stoic school of philosophy in Athens, so he led the Stoics.

clue.text: Covering traces of evidence, notorious villain running off

indicators.note: only a trace, the first letter, of each of the next three words is kept

parts.note: eloping is running off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A notorious villain covers the traces of evidence while running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traces of' gives ENV from evidence, notorious, villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping something all round is covering it completely.

clue.text: Flawed Republican alarmed hosts

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: alarmed means frightened or scared

explanation.surface: A frightened Republican plays host, and makes a hash of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' puts R inside SCARED.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface marked or damaged by an old wound or blemish is flawed.

clue.text: Unattached police on island

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Police officers are posted on an island without ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unattached' looks like single, but it means separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate and distinct parts are not attached to each other.

clue.text: Obliged to leave husband behind — the car can hold no more

definitions.text: the car can hold no more

indicators.note: the husband is to leave, so his letter is removed
the husband is left behind, taken out of the word

parts.note: to be obliged to someone is to be grateful or thankful

explanation.surface: An obliging driver leaves her husband behind because the car is full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave ... behind' drops H from THANKFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A full measure of fuel in the vehicle is all it can hold.

clue.text: Picked for team before start of season, showing guts

indicators.note: the team phrase comes before the season's opening letter

parts.note: a player picked for the team is in the side

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word season is used

explanation.surface: A player selected for the side just before the season shows real courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage, which the surface suggests, but it means innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts in the sense of internal organs are one's innards or entrails.

clue.text: Introduces fast way to travel round cape

indicators.note: the travel phrase goes round the cape's letter

parts.note: travelling in jets is a fast way to go
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Someone launches a fast way of travelling round a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts C inside IN JETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something into a system, as with a needle or new capital, is to introduce it.

clue.text: Contacts from East cut by ambassador (it's in old records)

indicators.note: the word is cut open and the other piece placed inside
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: contacts in the sense of phone calls
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Diplomatic contacts are cut short by an ambassador, as old records show.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'from East' means read right to left; the reversed word reads SLLAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Old 78 rpm gramophone discs were made from this resin, so it is found in them.

clue.text: Series featuring King George's vexation

indicators.note: the series includes the king's letters within it

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things
GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A series of events shows King George's annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed disappointment at being humiliated is a synonym for vexation.

clue.text: Yank is fool

definitions.meaning: a yank is a sudden sharp pull

explanation.surface: An American is called an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden tug is a sharp pull, and a stupid person is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Serious music disheartened grenadier on parade ground

indicators.note: with its heart, all its middle, removed only the outer letters of grenadier stay
ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dispirited grenadier marches on the parade ground to serious music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves GR from grenadier; 'ground' rearranges GR plus ONPARADE.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of opera is sung throughout on a serious theme, unlike comic or light opera.

clue.text: Time to leave local green

indicators.note: the time letter is to leave, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: a local person is a native of the place

explanation.surface: It's time to leave the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the village green but means inexperienced; 'local' is not the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone green is inexperienced, innocent and unworldly, so simple and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Understand speaker's refusal

indicators.note: a speaker says the word out loud, so a sound-alike is meant

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that the speaker is refusing.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp or be aware of a fact is to understand it.

clue.text: Press church to restrain island's senior politician

parts.note: a press is a cupboard, as is a cabinet

indicators.note: the church holds the island inside it, as if restraining it

parts.note: a minster is a large church
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: The press urges the church to rein in a top politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists but is a cupboard; 'to restrain' puts I inside MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the government's top team is one of its most senior politicians.

clue.text: Feature of footwear occupying prime locations in store

indicators.note: only the letters in the prime-numbered positions, second, third and fifth, of the word store are kept, so those in places one and four go

parts.note: the letters in positions one and four, which are not prime

explanation.surface: A shoe feature sits in the prime spots of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime locations' looks like the best spots in a shop but means prime-numbered positions 2, 3 and 5 of STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The front tip of a shoe or boot, covering the digits, is a feature of footwear.

clue.text: Messy drawing, possibly small fawn?

parts.note: to fawn is to crawl, behave obsequiously

explanation.surface: A child's messy drawing perhaps shows a little deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' looks like a young deer but is the verb to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy scribbled marks, which a messy drawing might be, are a scribble or scrawl.

clue.text: Square within enclosure providing shade

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
to square with something is to agree with it

explanation.surface: A square inside an enclosure gives some shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a shape or a place, but it is the verb meaning agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright yellowish green is a colour, and a colour is a shade.
